clue.text: Prosecutor gives account, having caught junkie

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a junkie is a drug user

explanation.surface: A prosecutor's case rests on testimony from a captured addict.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor brings charges against someone, which is exactly what an accusing party does in court.

clue.text: Seem a very soft audience

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
to have someone's ear is to have their audience

explanation.surface: A very quiet audience seems to be listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear to be something is to seem it, the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Hub of church rent asunder at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts the scrambled word in the middle of the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: asunder means torn apart, so the letters of rent are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The core of a church has been torn apart at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asunder' breaks RENT into NTRE, which 'at heart' puts inside CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hub is the central point of activity, its centre.

clue.text: A feature to watch, but it can be used

definitions.meaning: the hand on a clock face that marks off seconds is a feature of a watch
something used, not new, is pre-owned goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'to watch' suggests something worth looking out for; it is a feature belonging to a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep hand counting seconds on a watch, and goods that are pre-owned, both carry the same hyphenated name.

clue.text: Correct outfit, sexy but heartless …

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: hot means sexy

explanation.surface: The proper costume is alluring but cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the O at the centre of HOT, leaving HT.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms when describing an accurate answer.

clue.text: Rumour saw his personal stock diminished

indicators.note: the three words hold the letters in stock, and with the outer letters trimmed away what is left is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone saw their private shareholding shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock diminished' tells you the words 'saw his personal' store the answer once their outer letters are cut off: the last letter of 'saw', all of 'his' and the start of 'personal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisper, in the sense of gossip passed quietly around, is a rumour.

clue.text: … Dora may go the other way

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says that the letters of a route are put together wrongly, and done so they make the name Dora

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue before, a girl called Dora might set off in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis follows 'Correct' in 4 Down: the other way from correct. Read the answer as instructions and the four-letter route jumbled makes DORA; 'may go' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the incorrect route means heading the other way from the proper direction.

clue.text: Shakespeare's second best bed for a couple?

definitions.meaning: in his will Shakespeare's bequest of his second best bed to his wife begins with the legal word for a listed article
a couple in a romantic relationship are spoken of as a pair together

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's will famously left his wife 'my second best bed', the clause opening with the word for a listed thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A listed article in a will or inventory, and a romantic pair, share this four-letter word.

clue.text: Each child gets a pound for himself

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head
a son is a child
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: Every child is given a pound to spend on himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something personal belongs to an individual, done for oneself alone.

clue.text: Judge an instrument

definitions.meaning: in England a part-time judge in the Crown Court has this title
a woodwind instrument played by blowing, common in schools

explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales the title is used for a barrister sitting as a part-time judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a part-time English judge and a simple wooden flute.

clue.text: God in charge? There's no peace here

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity takes command, and tranquillity is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: where alarm and terror reign, there is no peace of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden fear and alarm is the opposite of calm, so a state of terror is a place with no peace.

clue.text: Get crime ring involved in the shape of things

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: O is a ring because of its round shape

explanation.surface: Getting mixed up in a crime ring shapes how things turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes GETCRIME with O, the ring, to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the study of shapes, so describing things by their shape is a geometric description.

clue.text: Scene for kitchen sink drama?

parts.note: kitchen sink drama is gritty domestic realism on stage; read literally, a kitchen garment suggests the part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink drama was a 1950s-60s British style of realist plays about working-class home life; the clue jokes that a kitchen garment names a theatre's forestage.
explanation.definitionFit: The forestage jutting in front of the proscenium arch is a playing area, a scene for any drama, named after the kitchen garment.

clue.text: Actor given space to find an exit

indicators.note: given here means the actor's word is handed something new in place of one of its letters

parts.note: a doer is one who acts
O, a nought, stands for an empty space

explanation.surface: A performer is allowed room to make his exit from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' swaps the E of DOER for O, the empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the opening through which you leave a room, an exit.

clue.text: Serving ace could engender grounds of complaint

indicators.note: could engender means the words may produce something new by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A tennis player's unreturnable service might cause the opponent to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could engender' rearranges SERVINGACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievances are wrongs that someone feels give them reason to complain.

clue.text: It's bloody hard to spell!

parts.note: a bloody event in the medical sense, heavy bleeding, whose name is famously awkward to spell

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' looks like a mild British swear word for emphasis; it is the literal sense, full of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy bleeding from a ruptured vessel is a medical bloody event whose name has a tricky double R and silent letters.

clue.text: What ticket machines do without change?

definitions.text: What ticket machines do without change?

parts.words: What ticket machines do without change?
parts.note: a machine that gives no change requires the precise payment, so passengers must offer the right money

explanation.walkthrough: 'do without change' reads as 'manage without change', i.e. machines that give none and want the precise sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticket machines that give no change demand the precise cost of the journey, nothing more.

clue.text: Spin spun gannet with expectancy

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of spin

indicators.note: spun means turned round and round, so the bird's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whirling seabird is in a state of anticipation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' rearranges GANNET into EGNANT; PR is public relations, the trade of putting a spin on news.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman expecting a baby is with child, so in a state of expectancy.

clue.text: Spirit wandered but made progress

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous spirit
roved means wandered about

explanation.surface: A spirit roamed about but got somewhere in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got better is to have advanced, made progress.

clue.text: Land badly in novel firework

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the novel

parts.note: a romance is a novel of love or adventure

indicators.note: badly signals the word land is to be put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone crash-lands in a story about fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns LAND into ANDL, which 'in' places inside ROMANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman candle is a type of firework that shoots out balls of coloured flame.

clue.text: Ring round one's friends

definitions.meaning: a ring is a round shape
a round is a ring shape or circuit
your social set, as in a close ... of friends

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ring shape, a round, and a social set of friends.

clue.text: Mean to have home care

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to care for

explanation.surface: Someone means to stay home and look after people.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, have it as a purpose.

clue.text: Queen involved in doctored seed

indicators.note: involved in means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: GM, genetically modified, describes crops whose genes have been doctored
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Royalty is caught up in the controversy over genetically altered seed.
explanation.walkthrough: GM stands for genetically modified, i.e. doctored; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the embryo part of a seed, as in wheat germ, so the word can mean a seed.

clue.text: Not against change, but this won't bring it about

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters in the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone not opposed to reform warns that inertia will never achieve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NOTAGAINST; the definition refers back to 'change': stagnation never brings change about.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of standing still with no development, so it brings about no change.

clue.text: Flock rose, say, over the diocese

indicators.note: rose means went up, and in a down answer rising reads the letters from bottom to top
over means covering or round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A congregation rose, say, across the whole bishop's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts EG round SEE, making ESEEG; 'rose' then turns it upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of birds of this kind is literally a group of them, the plural used for the flock.

clue.text: Entry of a headless dog

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a dingo is a wild Australian dog

explanation.surface: A decapitated dog makes its way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes the D from DINGO. The answer is a Scots word for an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish usage an ingo is an entrance or the reveal of a door or window, an entry.

clue.text: Saying about vehicle model having the edge

indicators.note: about means around, so the saying surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: an adage is a proverbial saying
a van is a vehicle
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A slogan about a particular car model claims it has a lead over rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VAN and T inside ADAGE; the Model T was Henry Ford's car.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the edge over someone is to hold an advantage, a superior position.

clue.text: It's revolutionary to take account of hidden wealth

indicators.note: to take means the revolutionary takes the account in front of him in this charade

parts.note: C/A, CA, is the abbreviation for a current account
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel gets the job of auditing secret riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' has CHE, Che Guevara, take CA, a current account, at his front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store of valuables, a hoard of hidden wealth.

clue.text: It's awkward to pedal without feet

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Cycling is difficult when you have no feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges TOPEDAL. The definition is descriptive: a young frog in the larval stage has no feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of a frog swims with a tail before it grows legs, so it lives without feet.

clue.text: Bow at the altar?

parts.note: Bow is a district of east London, and in a church the altar traditionally stands at the eastern end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests bending in prayer; it is the London district of Bow, in the East End, while a church's altar stands at its east end.
explanation.definitionFit: London's eastern districts include Bow, and the altar stands at the eastern end of a church, so both fit.
